examName: District Malaria Officers / Filaria Officers / Biologist, in the Directorate of Health Services, General State Service, Group-B
examPattern: Written Examination / Screening Test followed by Interview

topics: Parasitism: Concept, origin, evolution, advantages & disadvantages in the parasitic life.
Classification of parasites according to habitat.
Kinds of hosts: definitive, intermediate, primary, secondary, specific, paratenic, carrier, susceptible, resistant, accidental, reservoir, vector.
Modes of parasitic invasion, passive, mechanical, active, contact, transovarial, pathways of entry, sites of habitation.
Host specificity.

Habitats & environments of parasites: vertebrate digestive system, environmental conditions in different parts of the system, blood, reticulo-endothelial system, tissues & other microhabitats, invertebrate habitats.

Structural, physiological & biological adaptations of parasites for infectiousness, establishment & transmission, shape, size, attachment & protective devices, feeding aids, locomotion, respiration, metabolism, reproduction, life cycles, regressive changes, resistant & quiescent free living stages.

Host-parasite system: effects of parasites on hosts, mechanical, nutritional, destructive, toxic, biological etc. Hosts reactions to parasites: resistance, compatibility, immunity, cellular and tissue reactions, e.g. phagocytosis, inflammation, repair, abnormal growth, Humoral reaction. (Physiological resistance, immune response): premunition, avoidance of parasites by hosts, influence of host on parasite life cycle.
Disease cycles: concept of diffusion (dissemination), principles of control; protection of host, control in and outside the host.
Parasites & Zoonosis, vital rickettsial, bacterial, protozoan, helminthic & arthropod diseases. Leptospirosis, Leishmaniasis.
Vector Biology: taxonomic groups, methods of transmission, stages which act as vector, characteristics of arthropods in transmission cycles, effect of environment on vector transmission.

Study of the following parasites with respect to geographical distribution, habitat, structure, life cycle, pathogenicity, treatment and prophylaxis: 1. Trypanosoma Spp. 2. Leishmania donovani. 3. Plasmodium 4. Wuchereria bancrofti.

Insects as causes and vectors of disease & their life cycles in brief: (i) Mosquitoes (Anopheles, Culex, Aedes etc.), (ii) Rat Flea (Xenopsylla), (iii) Tse-tse fly (Glossina), (iv) Sandfly (Phlebotomus).
Insecticides: Classification, Chemical-nature, mode of action. Pesticide application equipment - Dusters, sprayers. Hazards of pesticides.

a) Principles and methods of insect control in brief e.g. mechanical, chemical & biological, Pheromones in pest control, Integrated Pest Control. b) Personal Protection Methods: Bed net & repellents etc.
Chemotherapy: (a) Antimalarial drugs, (b) Leishmanicidal drugs, (c) Antifilarial drugs.
Human Immunology, National Immunization Schedule.
Laboratory Examinations: (i) Collection of blood smear, (ii) Staining of blood smear, (iii) Examination of blood smear & identification of species.
Organisation and management of the Clinical Laboratory: (a) Setting goal & objectives, (b) Laboratory facilities, (c) Laboratory Set up, (d) Storage, stock inventory and checking etc.
World Health Organisation (WHO) - Objectives, Structure, Work & programmes.
National Health Policy, Health care system in India, National Health programme & scheme & particularly Malaria and Filaria.

importantNotes: The Screening Test consists of a single paper of objective type (multiple choice questions) carrying 100 marks of 1-hour duration.
No penalty marks will be deducted for wrong answers marked by a candidate.
Marks obtained in the Screening Test will not be taken into account for final selection, which will be decided on performance in the interview alone.
